NARB,OW ESCAPE.-- A man named Samuel Ather- ton, who drives a boat horse, narrowly escaped drowning in the canal at SA.nkey Bridges on Satur- day morning. He was; it is stated, attempting to jump from a flat on tO the towing path, wiien he fell into the water. A flat captain, named William Hatton, succeeded in getting- hirn out, but not with- out difficulty. Atherton, whenrescued, was uncon- scious, but was brought-round: A GENEROUS ACTION..—AR act of more than or- dinary generosity has been performed at 801 l on. During the erection of St. Stiviour's Church, the contractor, Mr. Collin, of Warrington, failed, and made a composition with hiS creditors of 6s 8d in the pound. The donor of the church, Mr. Thomas Greenhalgh, determined that nonne should feel that they had been the losers through the building of the church, and he has now paid the. remaining 13s 4d. The creditors are as surprised 'as they are gratified at this unexpected payment of their claims, which amount to a large sum. LO. OF GOOD TEMPLARS, WESLEY LODGE.--The usual Saturday night's entertainment of the above lodge was held at the Sankey-street coffee house, on Saturday. There was a good attendance of members and friends. The chair was taken by Brother T. Frian, and the following members. and friends gave a very good programme :—Songs by Sisters Daven- port, Sheath, and Grove, and Brothers Grove and Griffiths; recitations by Mr. CArdwell, Mr. Broad- hurst, and Mr. Buckley, Masterand Miss Jackson, and Siste.! Jackson. A short tc,--raperance address was given by a friend. A yen- pleasant evening was bronght to a close with a vote. of thanks to the chairman, and to Mr. F: BUckley- for presiding at the piano. _ _

• Sale at Heywas's of Boots and Shoes, to make room for winter goods-42 and 44, Horsemark.t-street.—Advt. • LOYAL ORDER OF ANCIENT' SHEPHERDS, ASH- TON LODGE.— The quarterly meeting of the late Spring Rose Lodge was herd" on- Saturdey at the house of Brother James Gleave,, Barley Mow Inn. After the usual business of the evening had been gone through, an interesting ceremony took place, in the initiation of Mr. R. W: Filincomb, J.P. Bro. Thomas Duckworth _occupied the chair, supported by P.P.C.S. James Parr, P:P.C.S: Edmund Wrigley, P.M Thomas Dennett, P.M. Henry- Devenport, Pro. Cor. See. A. H. Mather, and others.. Brother Duck- worth stated that it was a pleasure to him to pre- side and to have the honour of initiating Brother Francomb. Brother Francomb then addressed the meeting and dwelt upon the advisability of work- ing men joining such "societies, so that in case of sickness they would be provided with medical at- tendance, and a weekly allowance, and thus pre- vent them from having to appeal to the parish.for relief. In case of • death they were ensured of a decent interment. on the motion of Sec. Joseph Whitlow, a hearty vote of thanks was accorded to the newly initiated 'Brother for his address. WESLEYAN QUARTERLY MEETING. The quar- terly meeting of the Warrington Wesleyan Metho- dist Circuit was held on Monday in the Bold-street Chapel. The Rev. a E: Young, the newly-appointed superintendent, on taking the chair was accorded a very hearty welcome to the circuit. The other cir- cuit ministers, 'the Revs. G. E: Cutting and J. Howell Jones, together with the circuit stewards, IVlvsrs. Slice& and Starkey Smith, and a goodly number of other gentlethen were also present. The financial statement was laid before the meeting and considered ;to be satisfactory, and the return of members showed' a. considerable increase on the last quarter. It-was announced‘that the next May district meeting is to be held at Warrington, and also that during the present month a convention is to be held in this town for the promotion of Chris- tian work. A discussion took place with regard to day school work in Silver-street, and the question was ultimately. referred to a Jame and influential committee. The proceedings were characterised by great heartiness, and the friends present looked for- ward with confidence to the work to be done dur- ing the winter months, it being proposed to devote special attention to the villages of the circuit.—lt may be mentioned that on Thursday last week the local preachers' quarterly meeting was held in the vestry of Bold-street chapel. There was an un- usually large attendance, and the meeting was an exceptionally good one.. , • FATAL FALL DOWNSTAMS.—On Tuesday. after- noon Mr. W. T. Husband,,coroner, held an inquest at the. Unicorn Inn, Winwick-street, Warrington, respecting the death of Andrew Kilroy (51), who died at his residence in Dannett-street, Warrington, on SUnday morning, presumably from injuries re- ceived through falling doWnstairs on the previous night.--Ellen Kilroy; 33, Dolman's-lane, said that the body of the deceasul„which lay at 22, Dannett-,_ street, was that of' her father, who was a labourer by trade. He was 51 years of age. Witness went to the house of the deceased at about eleven o'clock on Saturday night, in company with a• relative. They found the house shut up. Witness heard de- ceased getting out of bed, and then heard a noise. With the assistance of a neighbour the doors were opened, and deceased was found at the bottom of !the stairs. He was lifted on to a chair, and asked Ifor a drink. Dr. Adams was sent for. Deceased died on Sunday morning. On Saturday night her father said that he was not hurt. His knee wan bruised and he was put to bed. He, slept until three o'clock on Sunday morning, when he had a turn for the worse.—Bridget McMahon, 28, Dannett- street, said' : that on Saturday night deceased was in her house until about ten minutes to eleven, when he west home. Deceased lived alone. He was sober, so far as she could see. About eleven o'clock witness heard deceased's daughter knock at the door, and afterwards assisted to, force open the door and place deceased, who was unconscious at the time, in a chair.—This was all the evidence adduced, a and the jury once brought in a verdict of ".Acci- dental death." CAIRO, WEDNESDAY.—The dervishes who were reported to be advancing from the south with the alleged intention of attacking the Egyptian frontier forces are now stated to I have retired to Dulgo' owing to rumours that the liabbabish tribe had returned to Delabeh and killed the dervishes at that place. The villagers as far as Sarrae do not appear to fear the dervishes, smell bodies of whom are visiting the villages in search ot dates. The inhabitants, however, are themselves suffering from want of food. All natives who have been questioned declare that the dervish leader Nejumi Is dead. Vutzttra, filmenay.—During the last 24 hours there kayo been 5 fresh cases at Trieste, 13 cases and 4 deaths at Pesth, 1 case and 2 deaths at Fiume, and 2 cases at Polo.
